gaps.construct: inst.update(msg) on whichever object is present, relying on duck typing across OpenSSL/HACL* HMAC objects and any hashlib hash
gaps.description: No interfaces, traits or dynamic dispatch; the two cases became a closed choice with an explicit `choose`. The digestmod can be any hash constructor, so `Hash` is a placeholder for an open set of types the doc cannot name.

gaps.construct: self._hmac or self._inner, where exactly one field is None
gaps.description: Expressible better than the original as a choice, but this redesigns the object's state rather than translating its two nullable fields.

gaps.construct: mutating an object reached through a field of self (an aliased reference)
gaps.description: The doc does not say whether a payload bound by `when` on an editable record is itself editable, or whether mutating a field's referent needs `uses`.
Became an operation taking the object as editable.

gaps.construct: msg accepts any bytes-like object (buffer protocol)
gaps.description: No interface to say 'anything that exposes bytes'; narrowed to Bytes.

notes: A two-line method exposes the main structural gap: no way to call 'update' on a value whose type is only known by what it can do. The choice-based rewrite is arguably safer (no None, exhaustive), but it closes a set that Python keeps open for any digestmod.
